ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a large triangle, and the three outer sides are all marked as three segments 1, 3, 1, so the total length of each outer side is 5. The gray region is located in the middle, and the unshaded regions are the small triangles at the three corners: one at the top, one at the lower left corner, and one at the lower right corner. These dividing lines in the figure are parallel to the corresponding sides of the large triangle, so the white small triangles at the three corners are all similar to the whole large triangle. Reasoning: The ratio of each white corner triangle in side length is 1:5, so the area of each white small triangle accounts for (1/5)^2 = 1/25 of the area of the whole large triangle. There are 3 such white small triangles in total, so the total white area accounts for 3/25. The gray area accounts for 1 - 3/25 = 22/25. Converted into a percentage, it is 22/25 × 100% = 88%.

raw_record.question_text: What percentage of the area of the triangle is coloured in grey in the adjacent diagram?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large equilateral/similar-sided triangle whose three outer sides are each divided into lengths 1, 3, and 1, so each full side has length 5. The grey region is the whole triangle minus the three unshaded corner triangles: the top corner and the two bottom corners. From the drawn parallel internal cut lines, each unshaded corner triangle is similar to the whole triangle with side-length ratio 1:5. Therefore each small corner triangle has area (1/5)^2 = 1/25 of the whole triangle. Subtract the three white triangles: grey fraction = 1 - 3/25 = 22/25 = 88%.
